title: Rudolf Blaschka sketchbook working-note and surrogate-delivery audit — pass 03
scope: Backend-only refinement of sketchbook pages 26-28 and digital-surrogate integrity. This file supersedes the provisional p26-p28 readings in the earlier crosswalk where they differ.
frontend_policy: Do not expose sketchbook images, thumbnails, page-derived geometries, or these working-note inferences on public GitHub Pages in this phase.
dating_guard: Pages 26-28 carry no secure written date. Do not date them to 1892 merely because the catalogue describes the sketchbook as circa 1892. Rudolf demonstrably reused the same Bremen hotel/agent network on his 1895 American journey, so later reuse must remain an explicit alternative until physical sequence, ink, or an independent dated reference resolves it.

supersedes.reason: higher-resolution visual reading, external historical controls, and a later-trip reuse guard

reading_confidence.Lange_Brinckmann: medium-high; Rudolf appears to reverse the historically attested firm-name order Brinckmann & Lange
reading_confidence.Obere_Strasse: medium; likely shorthand/variant for Obernstraße in the context of the following corner reference

external_controls.business: metalware factory; originated in Christian Baldewein's tinsmithing business
external_controls.source: Weser-Kurier regional-history article on Am Wall 165
external_controls.evidential_role: identity/location control only; it does not prove what Rudolf purchased or why he noted the firm

external_controls.business: gold- and silverware / jeweler with workshop and retail business
external_controls.evidential_role: strong corner-location control; the firm name Brinckmann & Lange was adopted in 1891
period directory control with resident, street, commercial and trade sections; exact Schüsselkorb 14 occupant remains to be extracted

spatial_sequence.working_hypothesis: The lines form a spatially coherent Bremen Altstadt sequence rather than unrelated place names: Am Wall -> Schüsselkorb -> Sögestraße/Obernstraße -> Markt.
spatial_sequence.guard: Distances are modern geometric controls, not reconstructed nineteenth-century walking distances.

dated_context_candidates.context: On the first American journey Rudolf stayed at the Central Hotel opposite Bremen station, visited the nearby shipping agents Ehrhorn, Emden & Mayer, and remained in Bremen until the following morning's special Lloyd train to Bremerhaven.
dated_context_candidates.assessment: plausible and presently preferred context because the catalogue associates the object with circa 1892, but the page itself is undated

dated_context_candidates.context: On the second American journey Rudolf again stayed at the Central Hotel, handled ticket business in Bremen, revisited Ehrhorn, Emden & Mayer, was recognized by the bookkeeper, and remarked that hardly anything had changed in Bremen in three years.
dated_context_candidates.assessment: real reuse alternative showing that the same Bremen logistical ecology persisted; cannot be excluded for p26

page_26.current_assessment: The note is securely Bremen-specific and probably records an urban errand/address sequence. Its exact trip/date is unresolved. Treat 1892-02-01 as a working candidate, not a dated fact.
page_26.interpretive_limit: Do not claim procurement of metalware, jewelry, tools, or travel goods. The businesses are identifiable, but Rudolf's purpose at each address is unknown.

page_27.diplomatic_reading: Von New York bis Bremen sind 880 geographische Meilen
page_27.interpretation: Rudolf was converting or simplifying a source distance of 3520 into 880 'geographische Meilen' by an explicit 4:1 rule. The notebook therefore records travel arithmetic, not merely a copied place-name.
page_27.journey_relation: Compatible with a New York-Bremen Atlantic passage on either the 1892 or a later American journey; the page itself does not distinguish them.
page_27.guard: Do not force the 880 figure into one standardized modern geographical-mile value. Rudolf's source unit for 3520 and the contemporary route convention have not yet been identified.

page_28.relationship: 27.5 cm is approximately 10.83 English inches, close to Rudolf's rounded 11-inch note.
page_28.interpretation: Practical metric-English dimensional conversion for a cylinder or cylindrical object. This extends the notebook's function from landscape observation and route calculation into measurement/translation between unit systems.
page_28.guard: The measured cylinder/object and date are unidentified. Do not connect the note to a microscope, specimen jar, shipping cylinder, model component, or other apparatus without a separate source.

pdf_derivative_metadata.assessment: The downloadable PDF is a later image-conversion derivative assembled after the 2009 digitization event, not the primary camera capture itself. Derivative-level ordering and duplication must therefore be audited rather than treated as physical foliation.

pdf_duplicate.finding: The two PDF pages embed byte-identical JPEG images despite separate PDF object references.
pdf_duplicate.interpretation: p13 is not independent evidence and the PDF is not a transparent one-frame-per-unique-leaf sequence.

older_backend_control.finding: The final 30 records of the older 700-frame Rakow OCR batch align with the current 30-page sketchbook PDF. Old records 682 and 683 already contain the same extracted image filename, matching the current p12/p13 duplication. Records 696-698 independently preserve low-quality OCR of the same p26-p28 working notes.
older_backend_control.interpretation: The duplicate predates the user's current PDF download and belongs to an earlier Corning/Rakow digital-delivery or processing chain. It is not a corruption introduced by the current local file.

digital_surrogate_integrity.catalogue_tempe_implication: Because the surrogate demonstrably contains a duplicated frame and the catalogue says the beginning sketch is Tempe, 22 April 1892 while the current PDF exposes Maricopa, 24 April as its first legible landscape caption, omission/reassembly in digital delivery remains a live explanation. Do not downgrade the catalogue to error without checking the individual JPG representation.

digital_delivery_target.known_public_delivery: Primo full display reports two digital representations: one PDF and 30 JPGs.
digital_delivery_target.technical_control: Ex Libris Alma Digital supports digital delivery and IIIF presentation at representation/file level. Once the item's representation identifier is recovered, its file list can be compared with the PDF derivative and older OCR batch.
digital_delivery_target.search_result: No representation ID for this sketchbook is exposed in ordinary web indexing. Other Corning records demonstrate direct Primo discovery/delivery URLs, but guessing an identifier would be evidentially unsafe.
digital_delivery_target.next_step: Capture the actual 'Zoomable view' target URL from Primo, extract its representation ID, request the corresponding file/IIIF list, and compare all 30 JPG identities/order with the PDF and old OCR batch. Priority question: does any delivered JPG contain the catalogued Tempe 22 April sketch?

functional_reassessment.knowledge_history_significance: The same portable object held visual, logistical, geographical and metrological work. It therefore documents the practical infrastructure of Rudolf's mobile knowledge production, not only its pictorial output.
